## How it works

- [statement] Apple's FAQ lists recurring rejection causes: incomplete app or crashes/bugs, app not performing as advertised, inaccurate screenshots, missing required user permissions, low-quality content. (medium confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/131256 · keywords: App Review process mechanics Resolution Center appeals and recurring rejection causes for utility and network apps · also: https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Apple's 2025 App Store Transparency Report: 9,100,620 submissions reviewed, 2,093,244 rejected (about 23%); rejections by category: Performance 1,354,418, Legal 495,673, Design 415,532, Business 283,820, Safety 151,159; 387,087 rejected submissions were later approved after developers addressed concerns. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02) — https://www.apple.com/legal/app-store/transparency/2025/ · keywords: App Review process mechanics Resolution Center appeals and recurring rejection causes for utility and network apps · also: https://www.theapplepost.com/2026/09/27/72747/inside-the-secretive-team-that-decides-which-apps-make-it-onto-the-app-store/
- [statement] Apple's 2025 report counts 26,305 appeals of app removals with 423 restorations (about 1.6%); this concerns removals, not pre-release rejections, so it is not a rejection-appeal success rate. DSA reports show 179 of 1,337 complaints reversed (Aug 2025) with median 15 days. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02) — https://www.apple.com/legal/app-store/transparency/2025/ · keywords: App Review process mechanics Resolution Center appeals and recurring rejection causes for utility and network apps · also: https://www.apple.com/legal/dsa/transparency/eu/app-store/2508/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Network-dependent apps are rejected under 2.1 when the reviewer cannot reach the back end or sign in (geo-blocked API, expired demo credentials, OTP the reviewer cannot receive, IPv6-only test network). This is reported by secondary blogs and forums, not stated by Apple as a statistic. (low confidence) — https://ptkd.com/journal/contact-apple-app-store-review-team · keywords: App Review process mechanics Resolution Center appeals and recurring rejection causes for utility and network apps

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Guideline 2.1 requires final builds, working URLs, demo account info and a live back-end service for any login; if a demo account is impossible for legal or security reasons, a built-in demo mode needs prior Apple approval and must show full functionality. Crashing or obviously broken binaries are rejected. (high confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ · keywords: App Review process mechanics Resolution Center appeals and recurring rejection causes for utility and network apps · also: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/131256
- [statement] Rejected or Metadata Rejected submissions are answered in Resolution Center; Apple says replies generally arrive within 24 hours and screenshots can be attached. Login instructions, feature locations and demo accounts belong in the App Review Information / Notes for Review fields. (high confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/131256 · keywords: App Review process mechanics Resolution Center appeals and recurring rejection causes for utility and network apps · also: https://ptkd.com/journal/contact-apple-app-store-review-team
- [statement] If still disputed after a Resolution Center reply, the developer files an appeal to the App Review Board via a link in App Store Connect / the Contact Us form; the appeal must be specific about how the app complies. Secondary sources report one appeal per developer account and a 14-day window, and no published turnaround (often a week or more). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02) — https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/131256 · keywords: App Review process mechanics Resolution Center appeals and recurring rejection causes for utility and network apps · also: https://ptkd.com/journal/contact-apple-app-store-review-team
- [statement] Guideline 2.3 forbids hidden, dormant or undocumented features and requires new features to be described in Notes for Review; an optional AI/alert integration should be explicitly described there, with how to enable it. (medium confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ · keywords: App Review process mechanics Resolution Center appeals and recurring rejection causes for utility and network apps · also: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/131256
- [statement] Mac App Store utilities hit Guideline 2.4.5: must be sandboxed, no root escalation or setuid, no login auto-launch without consent, no downloading code or resources that change functionality, updates only via Mac App Store. Apple denies temporary-exception entitlements such as com.apple.security.temporary-exception.sbpl allow iokit-open (CPU temperature readers) under 2.4.5(i). (medium confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ · keywords: App Review process mechanics Resolution Center appeals and recurring rejection causes for utility and network apps · also: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/111046
